unmapped_findings: The stacking fault energy (SFE) of the experimental steel is estimated to be 32 mJ/m² at -196 °C, compared with 40 mJ/m² at -77 °C and 61 mJ/m² at RT; a SFE of 32 mJ/m² at -196 °C still fully suppresses deformation-induced martensitic transformation (DIMT) but enables mechanical twinning.

Holding in liquid nitrogen at -196 °C for 30 min produces no isothermal martensite, indicating a very stable austenite; the initial as-forged microstructure consists of equiaxed grains with a fully austenitic constituent.
The alloy composition of this sample is Fe-20Mn-6Al-0.6C-0.15Si; its density estimated by the Kim et al. equation is 7.078 g/cm³ and the measured density is 7.114 g/cm³.

Note on scope: the tensile tests and Charpy impact tests at -196 °C were carried out on separate tensile-deformed and impact-tested samples, not on this sample that was only held in liquid nitrogen for 30 min and analysed by XRD; those mechanical/impact data therefore are not assigned to this sample.
